business.body:
- Sixth-largest pharmaceutical company in India by value (IQVIA SSA MAT Mar'26) and #3 by prescriptions (SMSRC MAT Feb'26), with 50+ years of legacy and a dominant position in anti-infectives, gastrointestinal disorders, pain management and supplements.
- #1 IPM rank in Anti-Infectives sustained for 15+ years; top-3 player in 4 of the top 7 largest IPM therapy areas; expanding presence in chronic therapies (diabetes, neurology, dermatology, urology).
- PAN is the biggest brand family in the IPM and ranks #2 in the IPM Top 300; the company has built 36 brand families worth over Rs.500 Mn each, including 1 family above Rs.10 Bn and 5 above Rs.5 Bn.
- Leading player in the Trade Generics segment; international presence spans the US, Latin America, Australia, Europe and other Asian markets.

business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Alkem is a Mumbai-headquartered diversified healthcare company built on a domestic branded and trade-generics prescription pharma franchise (housed under wholly-owned subsidiary Alkem Wellness), leading in acute and chronic therapies such as anti-infectives, vitamins and nutrients, pain management and gastro-intestinal, with growing presence in anti-diabetics, dermatology, urology, ophthalmology and respiratory care. Its international business spans regulated and emerging markets across the United States, Europe, Australia, Latin America, CIS, the Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia through own products, subsidiaries and partnerships. It is also building newer platforms in MedTech (orthopaedics and, via a proposed Occlutech investment, structural-heart/cardiovascular devices), biosimilars and Bio-CDMO (Enzene Biosciences), Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (Alkem Activa), and consumer wellness (ActivLife).
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Domestic Pharma (Branded & Trade Generics):** anti-infectives, vitamins and nutrients, pain management, gastro-intestinal, anti-diabetics, dermatology, urology, ophthalmology, respiratory care, Taxim, Clavam, Clindac
- **International:** cardiovascular, central nervous system, anti-diabetic, iron deficiency, pain management
- **Consumer Health (ActivLife):** A-to-Z brand portfolio (nutrition, women's health, paediatric care, everyday wellness)
- **MedTech:** orthopaedic implants and surgical solutions (Advita Ortho, erstwhile Exactech; Alkem Medtech Ortho, erstwhile Bombay Ortho), cardiovascular / structural-heart devices (proposed Occlutech investment)
- **Biotech:** biosimilars and complex molecules (Enzene Biosciences), Bio-CDMO development and manufacturing (New Jersey, USA)
- **API:** Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (Alkem Activa)

outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body:
- US strategy prioritises innovative/complex generics, including oral oncology and injectable products, with additional focus on biosimilars, as the US market shifts toward innovation and speciality products
- International emerging-markets strategy: replicate successful execution models from CIS and the Middle East across scalable markets, strengthen growth momentum in Africa, and restore performance in Southeast Asia through improved regulatory sequencing and focused launches
- Expand selectively into B2C (direct-to-consumer) branded generics businesses across new geographies
- Continue investing in regulatory, quality and operational capabilities to support the emerging-markets platform
- Enzene Biosciences pursuing dual-platform biologics strategy: a commercial biosimilars business serving India (with select assets out-licensed globally) and a CDMO business serving domestic and international clients via India and US (Enzene Inc.) facilities
- Enzene international biosimilars expansion via a capital-efficient out-licensing model, where Enzene develops and manufactures while regional partners handle in-country registration and commercialisation, generating milestone and royalty revenue
- The Company's Dividend Distribution Policy states it is deeply committed to driving superior value creation for all stakeholders and believes driving growth creates maximum shareholder value; it therefore first deploys profits to fund working-capital requirements, capital-expenditure requirements, reducing debt, and allocating reserves for inorganic growth opportunities, and only thereafter distributes surplus profits as dividend to shareholders.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY26 capital deployment centred on three new growth platforms rather than core-plant capacity addition. In MedTech, Alkem MedTech executed a binding term sheet (13 Feb 2026) to acquire a 51-55% controlling stake in Occlutech Holding AG, a Swiss structural-heart device specialist, alongside continued integration of Advita Ortho (erstwhile Exactech) and the newly acquired Bombay Ortho (renamed Alkem Medtech Ortho). In Biosimilars, Enzene Biosciences continued investment in capacity expansion, manufacturing readiness and international commercialisation, with its biosimilar portfolio approaching European launch readiness and US out-licensing opportunities evolving (Enzene's US Hopewell, New Jersey facility commissioning and Denosumab/Pertuzumab milestones are detailed in the strategy_outlook domain). In GLP-1, the Company strengthened manufacturing readiness and expanded strategic international partnerships to support launch and scale-up of its GLP-1 portfolio in India. Behind these, a digital-infrastructure build-out (Project EKAM, SAP HANA 2023, Project Aspire, and Level-2 MES integration across facilities) now supports a unified platform used by 22,000+ users. Management states the Occlutech investment (like the MedTech and Biosimilars investments generally) is being funded through internal accruals and existing cash, with no new debt and no equity dilution.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- US market is gradually shifting toward innovation/speciality products, prompting the Company to scout opportunities aligned with this shift
- USFDA streamlined the regulatory and clinical pathway for biosimilars development during the year, eliminating the phase 3 requirement subject to satisfactory analytical characterisation, reducing cost and development timelines — described as a multi-billion-dollar opportunity that could become a 'golden decade of biosimilars'
- International business delivered consistent growth driven by branded generics and strategic geographic expansion, and continues to offer long-term growth potential
- Emerging markets (Africa, CIS, Southeast Asia, Middle East and others) offer long-term growth opportunities in branded generics, supported by favourable demographics, improving healthcare infrastructure and sustained demand for affordable, quality medicines
- Emerging markets operate in a dynamic environment shaped by currency volatility, pricing controls, tender-driven demand and varying regulatory timelines; demand for branded generics remained resilient particularly in acute, hospital and high-volume segments
- Domestic retail generics business continued a downward spiral due to increased competition and uncertain supply logistics
- Key emerging-market challenges during the year included regulatory approval delays in select markets, pricing pressure, currency fluctuations and heightened competitive intensity in parts of Southeast Asia, addressed through portfolio prioritisation, calibrated pricing actions, disciplined working-capital management and improved regulatory planning
- Approximately 200+ regulatory dossiers filed in FY2025-26, enabling near-term launches across priority emerging markets
- Around 1,675 in-house product dossiers shortlisted for filing during FY2025-26 to FY2027-28, providing visibility for future portfolio expansion
- Enzene CDMO contract pipeline continued to grow across both India and US facilities, spanning clients across multiple therapeutic areas and geographies; Hopewell facility began reserving capacity for North American clients
- Enzene early-stage pipeline candidates in oncology and immunology under development, with evaluation of near-term patent-expiry opportunities ongoing
- Select Enzene biosimilar pipeline assets out-licensed for development/manufacturing by Enzene with commercialisation by regional partners in international markets
